title: 4.4. Tuples: Immutable Sequences
summary: Explore tuples: immutable sequence types defined with parentheses. Master tuple packing, sequence unpacking, and when to use tuples over lists.
learningObjectives: Create tuples using parentheses and recognize that comma notation defines tuples.
Understand immutability: tuples cannot be modified, appended, or deleted after creation.
Perform tuple packing and multiple assignment unpacking.

sections.heading: 4.4.1 Tuple Immutability & Syntax
sections.content:
A tuple is an ordered sequence of elements, very similar to a list, with one critical distinction: tuples are IMMUTABLE. Once created, elements cannot be added, changed, or removed.

Tuples are defined using parentheses: coords = (10, 20). A single-element tuple must include a trailing comma: one_item = (42,).

knowledgeChecks.prompt: How do you create a tuple with exactly one element in Python?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: A trailing comma is mandatory for single-element tuples: (42,) is a tuple, whereas (42) evaluates as parenthesized integer 42.

recap: Tuples are immutable sequences, safeguarding constant data collections against accidental modification.
